doc: A hand-made identity permutation (perm[i] = i): the corner hash is then (X + Y + Z) & 255, so sweeping the cell along each axis in turn (16 cells x 3 axes, fractions k/64 + 1/128) drives every gradient branch of the table in a predictable order. The permutation is the input plan0.perm (seed null). Same tolerance as perlin3.f32.random (measured spread 1.1e-7). The permutation input plan<i>.perm is the draw as recorded (256 entries for Perlin3, 1024 for Worley3); the kernel indexes it DOUBLED, concat(perm, perm) (512 or 2048 entries, so p[i + 256] = p[i]): a port that indexes the stored array directly runs off its end (see the .table cases).
